identity.task: R3 read-only Home and drum function inventory

what_current_already_does_well: Home keeps four useful performance controls visible and directly editable.
One key selects a drum track; one pad changes a step. Running with REC off defaults to selecting without an unwanted extra hit.
All eleven drum tracks and shared accent remain visible against sixteen steps, with selected row, playhead, out-of-length marks and lock notches.
Sound rows keep a stable K5–K8 mapping and fast K2 / repeated PARA navigation. Sparse rows keep the actual physical knob numbers.
Track mute is a modifier chord. Home part mute and pattern cue take one press.
A held step can cross from SEQ to PARA without losing its owner. Edited release preserves the hit; a stopped preview restores base values on release.
Pattern page, length, rate, part selection and pattern selection use separate controls.

gestures.control: One of the eleven inner black keys
gestures.effect: Always selects the track and rebuilds sound pages. It also auditions when stopped, REC is on, or KEY SOUND is ALWAYS. Running with REC off and default STOPPED only selects.
gestures.write: Only SEQ + REC + playing writes a local drum onset. PARA selection/audition never writes a hidden step.

gestures.effect: In SEQ, an empty step turns on at press. An existing step turns off only on release within 300 ms if unedited and still owned by the same target. A held or edited release keeps it. Input rejects only steps outside 0–63: a pad beyond the current loop length can still store a hidden hit. The loop length is not extended; the grid draws out-of-length marks.
gestures.write: This routing does not extend pattern length.

gestures.effect: Flips shared kit accent at that step. Accent is not a separate per-voice row.
Plays a loud hit. During running SEQ recording, writes the hit, shared accent and velocity.

gestures.control: PATCH held + black track key in drum view or drum MIX
gestures.effect: Changes that track’s vmute. With QUEUED MUTES enabled while playing, it toggles a pending change; repeating cancels it. Otherwise the change is immediate. PATCH release is consumed.

gestures.control: First five black keys while on Home
gestures.effect: Mutes 909, 808, BREAK, Bass B or Bass A in presentation order. It does not select a part. The configured queued-mute policy still applies.

gestures.control: White key / pad pattern press; hold two different patterns to chain
gestures.effect: First press clears a previous chain and cues a pattern. A second overlapping different press selects inclusive chain endpoints. PATCH + white does this from other views.
Directly selects pattern bank 1–16 or 17–32. This does not change pitch.
Moves one 16-step page, bounded to pages 0–3. Page selection is independent of pattern length.
One direction event selects an adjacent part in stable presentation order, bounded without wrapping. A part change cancels the held-step owner first.
Part views cue only the selected part. Home and other non-part views cue all five. This clears a chain and updates the displayed bank. The bass SOUND page has a separate preset exception.
K2 selects the previous/next sound row with wrap across existing banks. PARA advances one row. Four parameter knobs remain simultaneous. In a list, K2 chooses the row and K3 / < > changes its value.

gestures.control: Hold a step + K2, or the mapped arrows
gestures.effect: Applies in SEQ / PARA without an overlay. Chance runs 100, 95 … 5 percent, then conditional cycles 1:2 … 8:8. One direction event changes one position and marks the hold edited so release keeps the step.

gestures.control: SEQ: hold a step → PARA → current K5–K8; release original step
gestures.effect: SEQ → PARA preserves the owner. Only engine parameters belonging to that part can lock. Release in PARA finishes that same hold. A stopped preview restores base values on release. Going back to SEQ while held reports RELEASE STEP FIRST.

gestures.control: BT held + the target sound knob
gestures.effect: Forgets the relevant motion. With a step held, clears that step’s lock only. BT is consumed so release does not save.
Transport acts at press, not release. PLAY toggles start/stop. REC toggles recording. PATCH + PLAY redoes; PATCH + REC undoes; BT + REC asks to clear the part.

gestures.control: BT tap; BT + white; hold any button
gestures.effect: BT tap saves. BT + white copies live parts to a destination, with an overwrite question if occupied. BT + OCTAVE selects the destination bank. Help appears after 900 ms, or 400 ms for BT.

count_convention.press: One button, key or pad down plus release. Modifier chords count physical presses separately; a release is already included unless explicitly held.
count_convention.turn: One intended encoder-turn gesture unless explicitly counted as value events. Exact mechanical detents and elapsed time are unqualified.
count_convention.baseline: Starting state is explicit. Do not insert a menu or confirmation that current code does not require. Revised access counts remain unknown until the revised state/control reducer exists.
count_convention.rate_task: Four separated value events describe enumeration distance, not four required turn sessions.

evidence_limits: This helper did not run an emulator, native firmware, build, device, audio, physical LED or participant test.
No Git, source repository or PR mutation. All new files remain under helpers/drums.
Current 3c41 source is not a898 proposal execution. Historical 79280 captures are not current execution.
This helper captured no current firmware pixels. It extracted existing proposed 240 × 240 PNGs and inspected them at native size; it did not recreate or render them.
This is a function inventory, not independent acceptance. Fresh emulator reviewer admission remains with the parent.
Settings, the seven reserved CP1 external cases, CP2/CP3 policy and shared #891 remain outside this helper’s ownership.
New instrument identity pictures still need recognition/legibility review and current actual comparisons. Existing parameter pictures do not satisfy the new identity requirement.
